Code links point at the flat reading copies in [`code/`](code/), byte-identical to the files that ran and mapped to their as-run paths in [`code/MANIFEST.tsv`](code/MANIFEST.tsv); files without a reading copy (the game engine) link into Model 1's training tree ([`model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927`](model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927)). Both models read the same per-step arrays (the step cache stores them); they differ in which arrays they use and how they consume them.

## How to read this

- **Entity tokens.** Each decision step, [`data.features`](code/features/data.py#L283) calls [`observation.pack`](code/features/observation.py#L436), which emits one token per entity: the global clock, both farms, 200 tiles (own and rival), every worker (`CARRIER`), 12 shed and 5 seed `STOCK` items, 9 `MARKET` products, 8 `SHOP` types and 8 crop/animal `CONSTANT`s. Each token is an 80-wide row plus an 80-wide known mask (absent or hidden values are 0 with known = False).
- **Families.** Every other feature family adds columns to particular token types (`GLOBAL`, `MARKET`, `TILE`, `FARM`, `CARRIER`, `STOCK`) or per-worker *unit rows* (25 rows, farmer first) that the decoder reads when that worker's command is generated. A family leaves zeros on token types it does not describe.
- **Model 1** adds each family through its own zero-initialised `Linear` into the token stream ([`PolicyNet.encode`](code/model1/model.py#L748)); unit rows go into the decoder's per-worker queries. **Model 2** keeps, per node type, the source columns that vary within that type and projects them with a per-type `Linear` ([`compact_tokens`](code/model2/nf_format.py#L139), [`COLUMNS.json`](code/model2/COLUMNS.json)).
- **Transforms** in the column tables: `lin` = x / scale (tileclock clips to ±8, gaps to [-3, 3]); `slog` = sign(x)·log1p(|x| / scale); `rlog` = log1p(min(ratio, 1e6)) for a cost or sale as a fraction of own money; `flag` = 0/1; `clip` = clip(x / scale, -1, 1). Code: [`v8_cohorts.scale`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L111), [`v8_gaps._scale`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L112), [`v8_gaps._ratio`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L123), [`v8_tileclock.scale`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L449), [`calc_features.slog`](code/features/calc_features.py#L58), [`v8_dusk.slog`](code/features/v8_dusk.py#L99). Families without a transform column scale inside the expression shown.
- **Meanings.** Where a table shows *computed as*, the text is the code expression itself. Where it shows *meaning*, the text is the inline comment next to the column in the code, or the definition from the family author's column table (used only where the column name matches the code exactly).

## Solvers at a glance

The computations behind the columns. Most are exact replays of the game engine's rules from the actor's own view; none reads the rival's private state, the episode seed or future shop draws.

| solver | what it answers | inputs | code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price law and price tables | quote at any inventory; total receipts for selling or buying a run of units | market params, inventory | [`theorem_features.market_price`](code/features/theorem_features.py#L229), [`_Curve`](code/features/theorem_features.py#L260) (exact table ±2048 around I0 with prefix sums), [`engine market_price`](model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927/src/farm_neat/game/kaggriculture_engine_reference.py#L192) |

| No-action tile forecast | water/feed deadline, WEED/escape ETA, decay start, next production of each tile | one tile, step | [`plant_forecast`](code/features/flip.py#L115), [`_plant_no_action`](code/features/flip.py#L83), [`animal_forecast`](code/features/flip.py#L147) |

## Base entity rows

**How it's computed.** [`_world`](code/features/observation.py#L165) walks the actor observation in a fixed order (global; for each farm, own first: FARM, its 100 tiles, one CARRIER per worker; then shed and seed STOCK, 9 MARKET, 8 SHOP, 8 CONSTANT) and [`_Rows.add`](code/features/observation.py#L128) writes the header one-hots and each payload field as `value / scale`, never clipped. A field that is absent or hidden stays 0 with known = False; carried inventories are filled for own workers only. Field lists: [`FIELDS`](code/features/observation.py#L41), [`TILE_FIELDS`](code/features/observation.py#L36).

The actor view carries no order plan, so [`_state`](code/features/observation.py#L324) emits a single `CONTROL` token with only `commitments_known` = False set. Nothing in it varies, so Model 2 keeps column 0 for that type as a placeholder (`vary or [0]` in [`cmd_derive`](code/model2/nf_format.py#L365)).

## flip: no-action forecasts, jobs, reach, economics, price path

**How it's computed.** For every tile, [`plant_forecast`](code/features/flip.py#L115) and [`animal_forecast`](code/features/flip.py#L147) simulate that tile alone with no further action: [`_plant_no_action`](code/features/flip.py#L83) steps through yield-decay ticks (every 2 steps from `max_lifespan_step`) and day ends (unwatered counter, WEED at 2, ongoing production) for up to 3 days, giving the water/feed deadline, the WEED/escape ETA, decay start and the next production. [`_jobs`](code/features/flip.py#L170) turns each tile into one priority job and deadline (WATER_TONIGHT, HARVEST_DECAYING, WATER_TODAY, HARVEST, …). [`farm_view`](code/features/flip.py#L223) computes every worker's ETA to every tile as Manhattan distance + 1, routing FEED through the shed-access tile that minimises the whole trip (+2 to pick up and act) when the worker carries no WHEAT, then per-worker summaries and farm duty counts. [`price_path`](code/features/flip.py#L416) replays the next 6 passive consumption ticks (shops every 4 steps, town centre every 24) with no trades; [`economics`](code/features/flip.py#L383) computes hire (Fibonacci wage) and land affordability on raw integers; [`startup_rows`](code/features/flip.py#L479) certifies the fastest PLANT-then-WATER by two workers before tonight's refresh. Assembled per token by [`token_features`](code/features/flip.py#L516).

Model 1 reads columns 0-113 through one linear layer and uses the job kind and deadline only in the decoder reach bias; Model 2 keeps the varying columns per node type, including the raw kind and deadline.

## calc: market calculations

**How it's computed.** [`calc_features.raw`](code/features/calc_features.py#L74) builds on [`theorem_features.compute`](code/features/theorem_features.py#L651) (exact price curves, visible town demand, per-tile season units). Per product it projects the end-of-game inventory offset E = (inv − I0) + own supply (held + season units) + rival supply − visible demand − expected new-shop demand (WHEAT supply net of the animals' remaining feed), then P* = quote(I0 + E), the projected clearing quote of the marginal unit. The receipts of one more producer are the sum of quotes over the next `units` inventory steps from I0 + E ([`_Curve.total`](code/features/theorem_features.py#L287), prefix sums); net = receipts − input cost; n* counts how many extra producers still net ≥ 0 (cap 40); [`_k_sell`](code/features/calc_features.py#L62) binary-searches how many units sell above P*. Scaled with `slog(x, scale)` in [`compute`](code/features/calc_features.py#L170). Product rows sit on `market/<P>` tokens, the global row on `global` ([`data.calc_columns`](code/features/data.py#L269)).

## job routes (v6)

**How it's computed.** [`job_eta.extract`](code/features/job_eta.py#L25) builds direct ETAs (Manhattan + 1) from every own worker to every own cell, and resource ETAs for WHEAT and FERTILIZER: direct when the worker carries it, else via the shed-access tile that minimises the whole trip (+2) when the shed holds it. Nine job types per cell come from [`flip.job_bits`](code/features/flip.py#L456); WATER and FEED take their deadline from the flip forecast, HARVEST the earliest of decay, dehydration and game end. Per cell and job it keeps the minimum ETA over workers with a route. Token columns summarise each own tile's primary job; the FARM columns total tonight's feasible travel and count tonight's jobs with no route. Model 1 also feeds the per-(worker, cell, job) facts into the decoder as an edge bias ([`PolicyNet._v6_job_bias`](code/model1/model.py#L1006)); Model 2 reads the token columns only.

| # | token | computed as |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | TILE (own) | `True` |
| 1 | TILE (own) | `route` |
| 2 | TILE (own) | `bool(job_deadline_present[cell, j])` |
| 3 | TILE (own) | `min(2.0, eta / 24) if route else 0` |
| 4 | TILE (own) | `max(-2.0, min(2.0, ((int(job_deadline[cell, j]) if deadline else 0) - eta) / 24)) if route and bool(job_deadline_present[cell, j]) else 0` |
| 5 | TILE (own) | `float(route and bool(job_deadline_present[cell, j]) and (eta <= (int(job_deadline[cell, j]) if deadline else 0)))` |
| 6 | FARM (own) | `float(min_eta[tonight & route_exists].sum()) / 200` |
| 7 | FARM (own) | `float((job_present & job_deadline_present & (job_deadline <= flip.DAY - t % flip.DAY) & ~route_exists).sum()) / 100` |

## Decoder reach bias

**How it's computed.** [`flip.reach_matrix`](code/features/flip.py#L502) gives `reach_eta [25, 100]`: decisions for each own worker to act on each own tile, FEED on an unfed animal routed through a WHEAT pickup, 999 when no route exists. Model 1 ([`PolicyNet._reach_bias`](code/model1/model.py#L971)) adds, per decoder layer and head, a learned bias to each worker query's attention over own TILE tokens, looked up from (ETA bucket of Manhattan + 1, slack bucket to the tile's flip deadline, flip job kind) plus a `reach_job` bucket from `reach_eta`, plus the per-job edge bias above. Model 2 ([`NFlowNet.dec_context`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L450)) adds a learned per-layer, per-head bias from [`eta_bucket`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L54) (12 buckets of `reach_eta`) on the own TILE nodes.

## Same-step prefix and cash ladder

**How it's computed.** [`PrefixExecutor`](code/features/prefix.py#L49) starts from the actor-visible snapshot and applies the earlier workers' commands of the same step with the engine's own [`_apply_unit_action`](model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927/src/farm_neat/game/kaggriculture_engine_reference.py#L312). A PLANT that over-subscribes the seeds held at step start becomes PASS and the prefix is replayed from the snapshot ([`PrefixExecutor.apply_unit`](code/features/prefix.py#L86)). Before worker k decides, [`PrefixExecutor.unit_features`](code/features/prefix.py#L101) reads the state at k's tile, seeds left, blocked crops and shed room. After the workers, each market order updates per-product shed stock intervals [L, U] (SELL lowers both, buys raise only U) ([`PrefixExecutor.apply_order`](code/features/prefix.py#L227), [`PrefixExecutor.order_features`](code/features/prefix.py#L282)). The cash ladder ([`PrefixExecutor.cash_features`](code/features/prefix.py#L245)) replays the orders on a copy of farm and market with the engine's [`_commit_unit`](model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927/src/farm_neat/game/kaggriculture_engine_reference.py#L652), [`_do_hire`](model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927/src/farm_neat/game/kaggriculture_engine_reference.py#L702), [`_do_buy_land`](model1-b-even/code/trainer-v6/primitive-bc-v6-20260927/src/farm_neat/game/kaggriculture_engine_reference.py#L712) and price refresh, assuming no rival trades: money after earlier orders, affordable counts (product buys walk the price curve unit by unit) and a margin triplet for 17 thresholds. Training computes these along the teacher's decoded action ([`teacher_arrays`](code/features/prefix.py#L295)); play computes them along the model's own decoded tokens.

## Own last two turns

**How it's computed.** [`data.add_v6`](code/features/data.py#L421) stores the codec tokens (token, quantity) of the seat's previous two turns: each worker slot's command (only when it is the same hand) and the orders. Model 1 embeds them as history tokens and per-worker previous-command vectors ([`PolicyNet._history`](code/model1/model.py#L910)); Model 2 sums lag embeddings into a step summary and per-worker vectors that feed its fast and worker memories ([`NFlowNet.prev_action_emb`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L397)). At play the agent builds the same arrays ([`v6_history_arrays`](code/model1/model.py#L265)).

## v8 dusk

**How it's computed.** [`v8_dusk.raw`](code/features/v8_dusk.py#L179) takes the deadline (the dusk step 24d + 23, or step 718 on day 29 when nothing is deposited), each own carrier's load, its shed ETA (Manhattan to the nearest access tile + 1) and return slack. It simulates the day-end deposit in engine order (farmer first, overflow discarded) to get units lost if nothing changes, with min/max value bounds over the unknown order inside a carrier ([`_lost_value_bounds`](code/features/v8_dusk.py#L123)); then a queue where every loaded carrier walks home now and drops on arrival; then one harvest detour per carrier (walk, HARVEST, walk to the shed, DROP) with yield decay counted on the way. Values use spot quotes and calc's P* ([`unit_values`](code/features/v8_dusk.py#L111)). Shed-item columns sit on `stock/shed/<ITEM>`, globals on `global` ([`compute`](code/features/v8_dusk.py#L319)).

| 1 | `dusk_final_day` | on day 29: no day-end deposit remains |
| 2 | `dusk_shed_fill` | shed units (animals included) / capacity |
| 3 | `dusk_shed_room` | (capacity - fill) / 100 |
| 4 | `dusk_carried_units` | all own carried units / 100 |

## v8 cohorts

**How it's computed.** Scenario: full service of every visible producer on both farms. [`_entry`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L212) (via [`_plant_entry`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L135) / [`_animal_entry`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L179)) gives each tile's units by availability day, cached per tile state; [`_farm`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L228) sums them per product with bucket counts by time to first receipt. [`v8_cohorts.raw`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L369) then walks a sell-as-produced market path day by day: both farms' units of a product are sold together on the exact price law and split pro rata, animal feed is bought as WHEAT, and visible plus expected town demand drains inventory between days ([`_demand`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L342)). For one more producer of each kind ([`_new_schedule`](code/features/v8_cohorts.py#L263)) it finds the nearest site and route (DIG or BUILD first if needed), decides whether it can start today, and accumulates costs and receipts on the post-sale path to get cash to first sale, payback day and net to end; the receipts/cost ratio ranks the eight producers. Product columns (`m.`) sit on `market/<P>`, globals (`g.`) on `global`.

| # | column | transform | scale | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 1 | `m.own_first_le2d` | slog | 1 | # own producer tiles of this product, not yet producing; first scheduled receipt in 1-2 days |
| 2 | `m.own_first_3to5d` | slog | 1 | # own producer tiles of this product, not yet producing; first scheduled receipt in 3-5 days |

| 6 | `m.rival_first_le2d` | slog | 1 | # rival (public tiles only) producer tiles of this product, not yet producing; first scheduled receipt in 1-2 days |

## v8 tileclock

**How it's computed.** [`plant_sim`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L95) and [`animal_sim`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L158) roll one tile forward day by day under the engine's rules to the last day end, for four plans: full service, skip today, fertilize now, and fertilize on every day that raises the season (greedy interval cover). [`clock_table`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L193) runs the plant simulation for every crop and start day; [`clock_raw`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L216) reads off harvests, units, the loss from waiting a day, days to the next harvest-count cliff and to the last useful start, and value at today's quote; these sit on own empty TILE tokens. [`_plant_facts`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L255) and [`_animal_facts`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L296) give each producer tile's season units and the gain or loss of serving, skipping or fertilizing today ([`v8_tileclock.raw`](code/features/v8_tileclock.py#L357)).

## v8 flags

**How it's computed.** [`analyse_step`](code/features/v8_flags.py#L238) compares the seat's observations at t-1 and t (same day only) and attributes every inventory and tile change to the worker that caused it (one action per worker per step; DROP overflow simulated in worker order), giving per-worker effect codes, a per-product ledger (produced, consumed, bought, sold) and the cash split. [`_calendar`](code/features/v8_flags.py#L385) encodes the hour and day landmarks; [`_shop_block`](code/features/v8_flags.py#L411) dates every visible shop that consumes a product and computes the expected and worst-case demand from future uniform shop draws; [`_season`](code/features/v8_flags.py#L438) asks whether a producer started at the earliest possible step still yields before the end. Product columns sit on `market/<P>`, globals on `global`, unit columns on unit rows ([`compute`](code/features/v8_flags.py#L482)). Scaling is inside `compute`.

| # | column | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `lg1_produced` | units of this product entering own inventories by HARVEST (E L446-473) or COLLECT_FERTILIZER (E L515-522) in step t-1 -> t |
| 1 | `lg1_consumed` | WHEAT fed (E L505-513) or FERTILIZER spent (E L475-482) in the last step |
| 2 | `lg1_bought` | max(0, market_net): shed change minus worker deposits plus pickups (DROP overflow simulated in worker order, E L343-356) = units bought in the last step's market |
| 3 | `lg1_sold` | max(0, -market_net) = units sold in the last step's market (net of same-step buys of that product) |
| 4 | `lg2_produced` | same over the last two steps (t-2 -> t), both same-day |
| 5 | `lg2_consumed` | same over the last two steps (t-2 -> t), both same-day |
| 6 | `lg2_bought` | same over the last two steps (t-2 -> t), both same-day |
| 7 | `lg2_sold` | same over the last two steps (t-2 -> t), both same-day |

## v8 gaps

**How it's computed.** [`v8_gaps.raw`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L225) scans both boards ([`_scan`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L162), reusing the cohorts per-tile schedule) for cohort maturity and held yield; for the market it takes the first-order effect of one more unit in inventory (the quote drop between inventory and inventory + 1, which persists because town demand does not depend on price) times own and rival future units; every cost and sale is also expressed as a ratio to own money. The long block ([`compute_long`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L611)) carries one [`GapsState`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L339) per seat through the game: [`_update`](code/features/v8_gaps.py#L423) reconstructs a running cash identity for both seats (land, wages, seeds, animals, trade) from board and inventory differences, own per-product conservation, and the rival's net market flow over the last 24 and 72 steps.

## v8 lattice (Model 1 only)

**How it's computed.** [`compute_frame`](code/features/v8_lattice.py#L193) paints both farms as 10x10 grids with 40 channels per cell (tile kind, crop/animal, service flags, counters, workers, carried units, the flip job kind from [`job_kind`](code/features/v8_lattice.py#L94), shed geometry); [`stack_frames`](code/features/v8_lattice.py#L211) folds the frames at t, t-1 and t-2 into 120 channels. [`LatticeCNN`](code/model1/v8_lattice_net.py#L33) runs each farm through two 3x3 convolutions with a farm embedding and a zero-initialised per-cell output layer, and [`scatter_to_tokens`](code/model1/v8_lattice_net.py#L64) adds each cell's output to its TILE token. Model 2's `lattice_channels` is 0. Channel index = slot × 40 + channel (slot 0 = t).

## Model 2 graph: relation types, calendar, memory

**How it's computed.** [`NFlowNet.embed`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L365) builds 320 nodes: the 296 fixed entity slots from [`compact_tokens`](code/model2/nf_format.py#L139) (one per tile, worker, stock item, market, shop, constant, farm, global and control), FAST and SLOW memory nodes, 8 calendar landmarks and padding. [`relation_table`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L128) gives every node pair one of 17 relation types (general relations first, specific ones override); each relational block adds a learned bias per (relation type, head) on 4 of its 8 heads. [`NFlowNet.calendar`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L354) gives each landmark 6 features: offset / 720, target step / 720, past the end, log offset, target day / 30, steps left after the target / 720. [`NFlowNet.memory_step`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L419): a fast GRU (128) updated every step from a pooled graph summary and the actor's previous action; a slow GRU (256) updated at dawn from the previous day's mean summary; one worker GRU (64) per own worker slot from its carrier node and previous command, reset at dawn for hands. [`NFlowNet.encode_post`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L439) writes the memories back into the graph before the last relational block.

Rules run in source order and a later rule overrides an earlier one for the same pair, so the general relations (hub, memory, resource) only hold where nothing more specific applies.

| # | relation | pairs | assigned at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `other` | pairs no rule assigns, e.g. two tiles of one farm that are not adjacent | default (0) |
| 1 | `self` | a node with itself (assigned last) | [L183](code/model2/nf_model.py#L183) |
| 2 | `tile_adj` | two tiles of the same farm at Manhattan distance 1 | [L171](code/model2/nf_model.py#L171) |
| 3 | `tile_mirror` | the tile at the same (x, y) on the other farm | [L171](code/model2/nf_model.py#L171) |
| 4 | `farm_member` | a FARM node and the tiles and workers of that farm | [L173](code/model2/nf_model.py#L173) |
| 5 | `carrier_tile` | a worker and any tile of its own farm | [L174](code/model2/nf_model.py#L174) |
| 6 | `carrier_carrier` | two workers of the same farm | [L175](code/model2/nf_model.py#L175) |
| 7 | `custody` | an own worker and an own shed or seed STOCK node | [L177](code/model2/nf_model.py#L177) |
| 8 | `market_market` | two MARKET nodes | [L163](code/model2/nf_model.py#L163) |
| 9 | `shop_market` | a SHOP node and a MARKET node | [L164](code/model2/nf_model.py#L164) |
| 10 | `resource` | two nodes among STOCK, MARKET, CONSTANT and SHOP | [L162](code/model2/nf_model.py#L162) |
| 11 | `hub` | GLOBAL, CONTROL or a FARM node with any non-pad node | [L160](code/model2/nf_model.py#L160) |
| 12 | `memory` | the FAST or SLOW memory node with any non-pad node | [L161](code/model2/nf_model.py#L161) |
| 13 | `cal_later` | a calendar landmark and a later landmark | [L179](code/model2/nf_model.py#L179) |
| 14 | `cal_earlier` | a calendar landmark and an earlier landmark | [L180](code/model2/nf_model.py#L180) |
| 15 | `cal_resource` | a calendar landmark and a STOCK, MARKET, CONSTANT, SHOP, TILE or FARM node | [L166](code/model2/nf_model.py#L166) |
| 16 | `pad` | any pair that includes a padding node | [L181](code/model2/nf_model.py#L181), [L182](code/model2/nf_model.py#L182) |

Calendar landmarks in order: now, next shop tick, dusk, +2 days, +4 days, +8 days, +12 days, terminal (step 718) ([`NFlowNet.calendar`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L354)).

## Model 2 node columns

Model 2 builds a 674-wide source row per entity token: `rows` 80 | `extra` 152 | `v6_token` 8 | `x8_token` 354 | `knownness` 80 ([`SRC_KEYS`](code/model2/nf_format.py#L50)). [`COLUMNS.json`](code/model2/COLUMNS.json) keeps, per node type, the columns whose value varies across that type's tokens on a sample of seats ([`cmd_derive`](code/model2/nf_format.py#L365)); dropped columns are dropped identically at play time. Per-worker inputs bypass this: `unit_extra` 12 + `x8_unit` 41 feed the unit queries together with the prefix rows ([`NFlowNet.dec_context`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L450), [`NFlowNet.queries_teacher`](code/model2/nf_model.py#L484)).

## Training-only: no-op loss mask

**How it's computed.** [`training_unit_mask`](code/features/noop_mask.py#L121) replays the teacher's worker commands on the engine state in order and asks [`unit_reason`](code/features/noop_mask.py#L21) whether each one provably has no effect (a move off the board edge, an action on the wrong tile kind, a PLANT blocked because the step's PLANT requests exceed the seeds held, …), following the engine's own check order. [`teacher_supervision_mask`](code/features/noop_mask.py#L195) drops a worker's label only when it is a no-op in both the raw replay action and its codec encoding. Both models use it in the loss: Model 1 with `--mask-unit-noops true` (see `model1-b-even/STAGES.md`), Model 2 through `unit_loss_keep` in [`train.py`](code/model2/train.py). It is not an input feature and never a mask at play time.

## Built but not used by the shipped models

- **Theorem feature tokens.** [`features.py`](code/features/features.py#L41) packs 7,564 values per step from [`theorem_features.py`](code/features/theorem_features.py) and [`history_features.py`](code/features/history_features.py) into 22 feature tokens ([`feature_tokens.tokens`](code/features/feature_tokens.py#L140)). Neither shipped config has that input. `theorem_features.py` itself is still used as a library: its price curves, demand law and season arithmetic feed calc, cohorts and tileclock.
- **Long-lag history.** [`history_features.py`](code/features/history_features.py#L55) (lags 1, 4, 24, 72) is only imported by `features.py`.
- **Step search.** [`step_search.sample_rows`](code/model1/serving/step_search.py#L196) (best of k complete steps by joint log-probability) and [`step_search.beam_search`](code/model1/serving/step_search.py#L264) ship in both archives' agents, but both archives declare `decode: greedy`, so they are never called.
